right_definition: What proportion of counter-argument comments rely on third-person analysis of the issue (discussing the topic, people or the OP's position impersonally, without addressing the OP directly)?

Return 0 if neither appears. Generic CMV boilerplate in the title prefix 'CMV:' alone does not count. Ignore quoted text from others unless OP adopts it. right_definition: Does at least one comment by another user directly argue against the OP's stated view or its reasoning?

Return 1 if at least one comment, in its own assertions, directly challenges the OP's central claim or a specific premise/reasoning step (e.g., gives a counterexample, contrary evidence, or a reasoned objection). Return 0 if comments exist but none does (e.g., only agreement, clarifying questions, jokes, off-topic or meta remarks). Quoted text counts only if the commenter adopts it as their own objection. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates and reports of the outcome as evidence; do not treat them or thanks for changing a view as counterarguments. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null.

Validation must be directed at the OP personally, not merely agreeing with a point or generic politeness. Order within the comment matters: validation must precede the correction. Separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Use title and argument only to interpret the comment's target. Ignore quoted text unless the commenter adopts it. Do not count OP view-change/delta-award announcements, thanks after the view changed, or reports of the outcome as evidence. Generic delta-rule discussion is eligible but not itself validation. Return 0 if the list is valid but empty or no comment qualifies; null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.
right_definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments employ a concrete personal anecdote (the commenter's own specific experience) to argue against the OP?
right_spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). For each comment decide whether the commenter themself relates a concrete, specific personal anecdote/experience (particular events, people or situations they lived through) as part of their counter-argument. Use title/argument only to interpret what the comment is responding to. Do not count hypotheticals, generic examples, or others' stories/quotations unless the commenter adopts them as their own experience. Ignore any text announcing that the OP changed their view, delta awards, or post-outcome resolution updates; these are not evidence. Output = (number of comments meeting the criterion)/(total comments), a float in [0,1]. Empty list -> null; missing/malformed -> null.

right_definition: What proportion of counter-argument comments use second-person direct address to the OP (e.g., addressing the OP as 'you' about their view or reasoning)?
right_spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Generic 'you' meaning people in general, and 'you' inside quotations of other speakers not adopted by the commenter, do not count. Return 1 if at least one single comment first explicitly validates the OP's personal dignity, worth, or effort (e.g., praising their effort, respecting them as a person, acknowledging their sincere attempt) and afterwards, in the same comment, introduces corrective logic or a counter-argument aimed at the OP's view. Validation must be directed at the OP personally, not merely agreeing with a point or generic politeness. Order within the comment matters: validation must precede the correction. Separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Use title and argument only to interpret the comment's target. Ignore quoted text unless the commenter adopts it. Do not count OP view-change/delta-award announcements, thanks after the view changed, or reports of the outcome as evidence. Generic delta-rule discussion is eligible but not itself validation. Return 0 if the list is valid but empty or no comment qualifies; null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.
right_definition: What proportion of counter-argument comments employ at least one specific, concrete illustrative example?
right_spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). For each comment decide whether the commenter's own argument uses at least one specific, concrete illustrative example (a particular named case, event, person, situation, or detailed scenario used to illustrate a point). Vague generalities, abstract claims, and purely hypothetical generic statements do not count. Quoted OP text does not count; examples in quotations from other sources count only if the commenter adopts them as illustration. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Output number of qualifying comments divided by total comments (0 to 1). Empty list or missing/malformed input gives null.

Return 1 if at least one single comment first explicitly validates the OP's personal dignity, worth, or effort (e.g., praising their effort, respecting them as a person, acknowledging their sincere attempt) and afterwards, in the same comment, introduces corrective logic or a counter-argument aimed at the OP's view. Validation must be directed at the OP personally, not merely agreeing with a point or generic politeness. Order within the comment matters: validation must precede the correction. Separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Use title and argument only to interpret the comment's target. Ignore quoted text unless the commenter adopts it. Do not count OP view-change/delta-award announcements, thanks after the view changed, or reports of the outcome as evidence. Generic delta-rule discussion is eligible but not itself validation. Return 0 if the list is valid but empty or no comment qualifies; null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.
right_definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments contain specific numerical data or statistics (as opposed to only general assertions)?
right_spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). For each comment decide whether the commenter's own text presents specific numerical data or statistics as support (e.g., concrete figures, percentages, rates, counts, study results with numbers, dated quantitative facts), including numbers attributed to a cited external source. Do not count vague quantifiers ('many', 'most'), numbers that are not evidential data (list numbering, 'two reasons', times/dates used only as labels, usernames), or purely hypothetical made-up numbers. Exclude any text that announces an OP view change/delta award or reports the discussion outcome; delta-rule discussion is eligible but is not itself numerical evidence. Return number of comments meeting this divided by total number of comments, a value in [0,1]. Empty list gives null; malformed input gives null.

External sources cited as support count, without being treated as the commenter's own experience. Return 0 if comments exist but none does (rebuttals are abstract/theoretical, general principles, or hypotheticals without verifiable specifics). Quotations of the OP or others in background are not counted unless adopted by the commenter. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, thanks, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Empty or missing list: null (no comments to compare).
right_definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment by another user present a well-reasoned challenge to the OP's view?
right_spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments); use title and argument only to interpret what the OP claims. Return 1 if at least one comment gives a well-reasoned counterargument to the OP's stated view: it targets the OP's claim with explicit reasoning or evidence that is logically coherent and relevant. Return 0 if comments are present but none do (e.g., insults, jokes, bare assertions, off-topic, clarification-only). Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates and reports of the outcome; they are not evidence of reasoning quality. Do not use comment order as rank or chronology. Quoted text counts only if the commenter adopts it as their own argument.

Return 1 if at least one single comment both (a) explicitly acknowledges that the OP's initial premise (or its starting premise/basic point) is valid, correct, reasonable or true, in the commenter's own voice (not merely quoting the OP or a third party without adopting it), and (b) afterwards within that same comment introduces a point of disagreement or divergence (e.g. 'but', 'however', a different consideration). Acknowledgment must come before the divergence in the comment text. Both conditions must co-occur in the same comment; separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Return 0 if no comment qualifies, including generic politeness without validating the premise, or agreement with no divergence. Empty comment list gives 0; missing/malformed OC_comments gives null. Ignore any text announcing that the OP changed their view, delta awards, or post-outcome resolution updates; do not treat them as evidence. Generic discussion of delta/platform rules is eligible but is not itself acknowledgment of the premise.
right_definition: Does the OP's argument text contain at least one explicit hedging or self-doubt marker in the OP's own voice?
right_spec: Read only the argument column (OP's text). Return 1 if the OP's own assertions contain at least one explicit hedge or self-doubt marker (e.g., 'I might be wrong', 'maybe', 'perhaps', 'I'm not sure', 'it seems to me', 'I could be mistaken', 'I'm unsure', 'probably'), applied to the OP's own claims. Return 0 if the argument is presented without any such markers (unwavering certainty). Ignore hedges inside quotations attributed to other people unless the OP adopts them. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits/updates and reports of the outcome (e.g., 'EDIT: my view has changed', 'delta awarded') as evidence; do not count them. Generic discussion of platform rules is eligible. Return null if argument is missing or malformed; empty text gives null.

left_definition: Does the original poster's argument text contain at least one explicit marker of uncertainty about their own view or claims?
left_spec: Read only the `argument` column (OP's argument body; not title, comments or conversation). Return 1 if the OP, in their own assertions, uses at least one explicit uncertainty marker about their own view or claims (e.g., 'I'm not sure', 'maybe', 'perhaps', 'I might be wrong', 'I could be mistaken', 'it seems', 'I think' used as hedging, 'probably', 'I'm unsure'). Return 0 if none are present. Do not count uncertainty markers inside quotations from other speakers unless the OP adopts them as their own. Ignore view-change or delta-award announcements, edits reporting the outcome, and post-outcome resolution updates (e.g., 'EDIT: my view has changed', 'Delta awarded'); these are not evidence. Generic discussion of platform/delta rules is eligible but only counts if it contains an uncertainty marker by the OP. Uncertainty about external facts that is not hedging of the OP's claims still counts only if explicitly marked as OP's own uncertainty. Return null if argument is missing or malformed; return 0 for empty text.
right_definition: Does the original poster's own argument text explicitly acknowledge a counter-argument or a limitation of their own view?
right_spec: Read the OP's title and argument (current text). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly acknowledges a possible counter-argument, opposing consideration, exception, weakness or limitation of their own view (e.g., 'I know some will say...', 'a weakness of my view is...', 'admittedly...'). Return 0 if no such explicit acknowledgement exists. Do not count quotations or background views attributed to others unless the OP adopts them as a counterpoint to their own view. Exclude any OP view-change, delta-award announcements, edits reporting the outcome or post-outcome resolution updates (e.g., 'EDIT: my view was changed', 'Δ'); these are not evidence. Generic discussion of subreddit/delta rules does not count as acknowledgement. Return null if argument is missing or malformed; empty text gives 0.

Return null if argument is missing or malformed; return 0 for empty text.
right_definition: Do the counter-argument comments rely solely on abstract logical refutation, with no reference to any specific named external program or location?
right_spec: Parse OC_comments (comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if the list is non-empty, at least one comment makes a counter-argument by abstract reasoning (logical refutation, principles, hypotheticals, conceptual distinctions), and NO comment refers to a specific proper-named external program or named location. Return 0 if any comment references a specific named program or location, or if no comment offers abstract logical refutation (e.g., only other kinds of content). Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome. Null if the list is empty, missing or malformed (no comparison group defined).

Return 1 if the OP, in their own assertions, uses at least one explicit uncertainty marker about their own view or claims (e.g., 'I'm not sure', 'maybe', 'perhaps', 'I might be wrong', 'I could be mistaken', 'it seems', 'I think' used as hedging, 'probably', 'I'm unsure'). Return 0 if none are present. Do not count uncertainty markers inside quotations from other speakers unless the OP adopts them as their own. Ignore view-change or delta-award announcements, edits reporting the outcome, and post-outcome resolution updates (e.g., 'EDIT: my view has changed', 'Delta awarded'); these are not evidence. Generic discussion of platform/delta rules is eligible but only counts if it contains an uncertainty marker by the OP. Uncertainty about external facts that is not hedging of the OP's claims still counts only if explicitly marked as OP's own uncertainty. Return null if argument is missing or malformed; return 0 for empty text.
right_definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment by another user cite a specific empirical example (e.g., a concrete real-world case, event, study or data point) in support of its counter to the OP's view?
right_spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments). Use title and argument only to understand what the OP's view is. Return 1 if at least one comment, in its own assertion, argues against the OP's view and cites a specific empirical example as support (a named or concretely described real-world case, event, study, statistic or data point; an external source cited as support counts). Exclude OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates and reports of the outcome; these are not evidence. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null.

For each comment decide whether, within that same comment, the commenter first explicitly acknowledges that the OP's position/reasoning has validity (e.g. 'you're right that...', 'this is a fair point') AND THEN introduces a narrower, specific caveat, exception or qualification (not a blanket rejection). Use title and argument only to interpret the comment's target. Acknowledgement of something other than the OP's view, or acknowledgement without a following specific caveat, does not count. Ignore quoted text unless the commenter adopts it. Exclude any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome as evidence. Output = (number of qualifying comments)/(total comments), a number in [0,1]. Empty list -> null; malformed/missing -> null.

right_definition: Does the original argument explicitly ask the community for feedback or advice?

Return 1 if the OP's own text explicitly requests feedback, advice, input, opinions or responses from the community/readers (e.g., 'please tell me what you think', 'I'd appreciate advice', 'help me see this differently'). Return 0 if no such explicit request is present. Merely stating a view, or the generic CMV invitation implied by the forum, does not count; the request must be written in the text. Do not count quoted text from other people unless the OP adopts it as their own request. Ignore and do not count OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits/updates, or reports of the outcome (e.g., 'EDIT: my view was changed', 'delta awarded', 'thanks for the responses that changed my mind') as evidence. Return null if argument is missing or malformed; empty text gives 0.

right_definition: What share of the counter-argument comments contain at least one concrete, locally verifiable example (specific case, instance, data point or experience) offered in support of the commenter's counter-argument?

Return 1 if at least one comment itself uses an analogy comparing the OP's issue to a different, familiar or everyday scenario (e.g., 'it's like ...', a parallel everyday situation) to support its counter-argument; return 0 if none do. Count only the commenter's own analogies, not analogies merely quoted from others and rebutted without adoption. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, thanks for changed view, or reports of the outcome as evidence. Literal examples of the topic itself are not analogies. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed input gives null.
right_definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments contain specific numerical data or statistics (as opposed to only general assertions)?
right_spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). For each comment decide whether the commenter's own text presents specific numerical data or statistics as support (e.g., concrete figures, percentages, rates, counts, study results with numbers, dated quantitative facts), including numbers attributed to a cited external source. Do not count vague quantifiers ('many', 'most'), numbers that are not evidential data (list numbering, 'two reasons', times/dates used only as labels, usernames), or purely hypothetical made-up numbers. Exclude any text that announces an OP view change/delta award or reports the discussion outcome; delta-rule discussion is eligible but is not itself numerical evidence. Return number of comments meeting this divided by total number of comments, a value in [0,1]. Empty list gives null; malformed input gives null.

For each comment decide whether, within that same comment, the commenter first explicitly acknowledges that the OP's position/reasoning has validity (e.g. 'you're right that...', 'this is a fair point') AND THEN introduces a narrower, specific caveat, exception or qualification (not a blanket rejection). Use title and argument only to interpret the comment's target. Acknowledgement of something other than the OP's view, or acknowledgement without a following specific caveat, does not count. Ignore quoted text unless the commenter adopts it. Exclude any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome as evidence. Output = (number of qualifying comments)/(total comments), a number in [0,1]. Empty list -> null; malformed/missing -> null.

Quoted OP text does not count; examples in quotations from other sources count only if the commenter adopts them as illustration. right_definition: Are all comments received by the OP supportive of the OP's view, with none opposing it?

For each comment decide whether, within that same comment, the commenter first explicitly acknowledges that the OP's position/reasoning has validity (e.g. 'you're right that...', 'this is a fair point') AND THEN introduces a narrower, specific caveat, exception or qualification (not a blanket rejection). Use title and argument only to interpret the comment's target. Acknowledgement of something other than the OP's view, or acknowledgement without a following specific caveat, does not count. Ignore quoted text unless the commenter adopts it. Exclude any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome as evidence. Output = (number of qualifying comments)/(total comments), a number in [0,1]. Empty list -> null; malformed/missing -> null.
right_definition: Do the counter-argument comments introduce at least one concrete, external factual analogy (coded 1), as opposed to relying solely on abstract logical refutation (coded 0)?
right_spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' counter-argument comments; order carries no meaning). Use title/argument only to interpret what a comment targets. Group A (output 1): at least one comment, in the commenter's own voice, introduces a concrete, external factual analogy, i.e. a specific real-world case, example, historical event, empirical fact or comparable real situation outside the OP's own scenario, used as an analogy or comparison to challenge the OP's view. Group B (output 0): the comments contain counter-argument material, but ALL of it is abstract logical refutation (reasoning, definitions, logical structure, hypotheticals without concrete real-world referents) and no comment introduces a concrete external factual analogy. If both kinds occur, output 1 (A takes precedence). Output null if OC_comments is empty/missing/malformed or contains no counter-argument reasoning of either type (neither group). Ignore quoted text from others unless the commenter adopts it. Exclude, as evidence for either group, any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates or reports of the outcome. Generic delta-rule discussion is not evidence of either group.

Quotations of the OP or of material merely being rebutted do not count unless the commenter adopts them as support. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates or reports of the outcome; they are not evidence. Return 0 if the list is valid but empty or no comment qualifies; null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.
